newsitem.title: USA: Depression in Caribbean forecast to strengthen.
newsitem.headline: Depression in Caribbean forecast to strengthen.

text.p: A tropical depression that developed Tuesday in the western Caribbean was expected to strengthen as it continued moving northwest toward Cuba, the National Hurricane Center said.

At 1100 EDT/1500 GMT, the center of tropical depression twelve was near latitude 16.1 north and longitude 83.0 west, or about 110 miles (175 km) south-southeast of Swan Island, or about 490 miles (790 km) south of Havana, Cuba.

The depression was moving northwest at nearly 10 mph (17 kph), and this was expected to continue through Tuesday night. Maximum sustained winds were near 35 mph (55 kph) and strengthening to a tropical storm was likely later Tuesday.

"All interests in the northwestern Caribbean, Cuba, the eastern Gulf of Mexico, and Florida should closely monitor the progress of this developing system," National Hurricane Center said. "A hurricane watch could be issued for western Cuba as early as this afternoon."
The depression would become Tropical Storm Lili if maximum sustained winds reached 39 mph (62 kph). It would become a hurricane if such winds reached 74 mph (119 kph).
